subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK, command-cron, and skill-command paths, and what owner/auth/config gates are required for host filesystem, exec/session/control-plane, generic slash-command, CLI, and startup-readiness access?
rationale: The unresolved work can expose privileged process, filesystem, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Land narrow gated slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK, command cron, and skill-owned tool dispatch sufficient for now, and reject broader host-FS, exec, slash-command, and CLI dispatch until a sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on dangerous-tool and Gateway operator-boundary policy where recent history points to this owner.
